doc.title: Peter Vacher interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001

chapter: Joe Darensbourg and the Creole question
title: Taping Joe Darensbourg around his wife
summary: Darensbourg's three marriages, and how Vacher recorded his stories in the car and supermarket to avoid his third wife's editing.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Who is the fellow you had to take into the grocery store?
What was the reason for that?

Well Joe was quite a colorful character, and if you read this book you’ll say the ways in which he was colorful. Joe was a Creole from Louisiana who was first married to a Creole woman, well basically because he put her in the family way, secondly he was married to a black lady, and thirdly he was married to a white woman. So as he always said to me, he covered all bases as you would put it. And the third Mrs. Darensbourg, who is a very nice lady, but I think she was from North Carolina, quite straight laced. And to be honest, she was the one that saw to the later years of Joe and to his considerable success and prosperity. She managed his life in a way that put him on the straight and narrow. But she was a bit straight laced. And when we got talking about some of his more nefarious activities, particularly his various sexual liaisons and things like that, I think I told you the other evening, in the background of the tapes you can hear her saying, “He doesn’t want to know about that, Joe.” Well he did want to know about it. So we found ways to kind of continue to tape recording in unusual places, including the car when he was driving me around, and this particular occasion when we went round the supermarket while he was collecting the groceries. So I was interviewing him while he was sort of collecting the cereal and the bits and pieces. And that way we got ‘round his wife kind of putting an editorial hand on things.
